title: XENIA Arrival 0.1 two-visit fixture development draft
description: A record of up to five GET exchanges with one host: an orientation, a view address asked without a credential, a view, a later view, and a view asked with a cursor the host did not hand back. Each exchange is optional. A response body is any JSON object or null, so a malformed host document is a failed check and not a broken fixture. There is no slot for headers or for the credential. A fixture is the recorder's account; matching this schema does not establish that any host sent these exchanges, that one reader made both visits, or that time passed between them.

origin.description: How the fixture came to be: written by hand, the bytes a host sent, or a host's answers mapped into these shapes by the recorder.

acknowledged_by_recorder.description: The recorder's own statement of whether it acknowledged anything between the two views. It says nothing about other holders of the same credential.

cursor.description: Opaque to the caller. Whether it is self-contained or a key to state the host keeps is not stated.

requested_at.description: When the recorder sent the request, by the recorder's clock.

href.description: The address asked, without the cursor.

credential.description: Whether a credential was presented. The credential itself is never recorded.

cursor.description: The cursor presented with the request, or null.

body.description: The JSON object the host answered with, or null when it answered with none.
